rationale: X is at parity overall: it derives the correct `TimeZone#local` to `TimeWithZone` path and supplies all seven requested cases with local, UTC, abbreviation, DST, offset, failure-mode, evidence, and narrow-command coverage. Re-running its focused `test/time_zone_test.rb` filter produced 6 runs, 22 assertions, and 0 failures, while a focused runtime probe confirmed every proposed observable. The minor Moscow-history label error and several mistargeted line links do not alter the proposed assertions or preservation gate.

shortcomings.summary: X mislabels Moscow's pre-transition UTC+4 period as `MSD`; the selected +03:00 assertions remain correct.
shortcomings.evidence: An executed `periods_for_local(Time.utc(2014, 10, 26, 1))` check printed [`MSK`, false, 14400] and [`MSK`, false, 10800], so both ambiguous periods are `MSK` in this checkout.

shortcomings.summary: Several citations in X.md miss the lines containing the claimed code.
shortcomings.evidence: X.md links `#zone` to `activesupport/lib/active_support/time_with_zone.rb` L126-L128 although the method is at L138-L140, links `#<=>` to L209-L211 although it is at L245-L248, and cites the Hawaii mapping at `activesupport/lib/active_support/values/time_zone.rb` L42 although it is at L38; R1/R2 use the correct locations.

shortcomings.summary: X did not retry its failed direct enumeration of the ambiguous Moscow and Eastern periods, though the requested behavior was already resolved by other checks.
shortcomings.evidence: X.thread.md's last direct period-enumeration command ended in `NoMethodError`, while R1.thread.md completed that probe; before the failure, X had already measured every selected result and run the focused suite.

strengths.summary: X performed stronger automated verification than R2 by executing the exact six-test preservation filter.
strengths.evidence: X.thread.md records `6 runs, 22 assertions, 0 failures`; R2.thread.md records a runtime-value probe but not execution of that focused test filter.

strengths.summary: X makes especially clear why the spring-gap case must assert more than the UTC instant.
strengths.evidence: X.md explains that UTC `07:00Z` alone cannot distinguish the valid 03:00 EDT shift from retaining an invalid 02:00 wall clock with the EDT offset, motivating explicit local-component, abbreviation, and DST assertions.
